collection.description: A villager is on watch at the lookout rock when a sudden squall comes over the ridge, all wind and rain and lightning.

ask.text:
(Name) is on watch at the lookout rock when a sudden squall comes over the ridge, all wind and rain and lightning. The lookout has a little lean-to of palm leaves, and a long flat rock where the watchers lie to see the sea.
Lightning is hitting the ridge, closer each time. (Name) can shelter in the lean-to, or run down the hill to the village through the open grass.
What should (name) do?

c1o1.text: Lightning strikes the lookout rock a body length away. (Name) is thrown against the post of the lean-to and lies there stunned until the squall passes. (He/She) walks down to the village, singed and shaky, and knows everybody and everything, except (his/her) own name, which the flash seems to have burned away. It never comes back. The village calls (him/her) "?".

c1o2.text: The lean-to holds. The lightning moves on over the sea. (Name) crawls out, soaked and alive, and sees, far out on the water, a canoe that had been caught in the squall, heading safely for the reef. (He/She) waves both arms until they see (him/her), and guides them in by shouting.

c1.text: (Name) crawls under the palm leaves and curls up small. The rain roars on the leaves. Then the whole world goes white...

c2o1.text: (Name) makes it home, drenched and shaking, as the lightning walks across the hill behind (him/her). (He/She) has always loved the rain, standing in it with (his/her) face up. Not anymore. From then on, at the first drop, (he/she) is indoors, and listens to the storms from under (his/her) blanket.

c2o2.text: (Name) makes it home, drenched and laughing with relief, and stands in the doorway watching the lightning walk away over the sea. "That," (he/she) says to anyone who will listen, "was the best run of my life."

c2.text: (Name) runs down through the long grass, rain in (his/her) eyes, the thunder right on top of (him/her)...
